summary: You engaged the scenario well, identifying several stakeholders and drawing on relevant external cases such as the NHS HSSIB investigation and Volkswagen, along with EACE code references. The main gaps are an internal contradiction between your conclusion (Not Ship) and your recommendation (accept the government contract), weak treatment of the case for shipping, and the missing abstract. Addressing these would strengthen the report considerably.
next_steps: Align your recommendation with your conclusion: state explicitly the conditions under which shipping would be acceptable, such as verified fixes, disclosure to the health department, or a risk threshold, and justify them with evidence.
Strengthen the case for shipping by supporting it with evidence rather than assertion, and clearly separate physical-harm risks from data-loss risks, justifying any failure-rate figure you use.
Add the missing abstract, include at least one figure or table to support your analysis, and complete all references with full details, including URLs and accessed dates.

criteria.C1: You identified several relevant ethical issues and linked them to engineering design and professional duty, earning Very good. To reach Excellent, deepen the link between the issues and the design context, and explain how each stakeholder's interests differ (for example, the health department versus end-users). Introducing the physical-harm versus data-loss distinction in your introduction would also help.
criteria.C2: You presented arguments on both sides, but the case for shipping is largely asserted and your discussion is weighted towards the case against. To reach Excellent, give the arguments for shipping real depth, and provide decision-making recommendations for several stakeholders, not mainly Rachel and her company.
criteria.C3: Your report has a logical structure, but the conclusion and recommendation conflict, which weakens the overall argument. Resolve this contradiction and ensure every paragraph links clearly to the conclusion. This would make your argument more compelling and move you towards Very good or Excellent.
criteria.C4: You used relevant external case studies and EACE references, with some quantitative illustration, earning Very good. To reach Excellent, substantiate your figures properly, such as justifying the 1% failure assumption, add a balanced range of qualitative and quantitative evidence, and use stronger sources for the Apple argument. Also qualify the link between the NHS incident and your scenario more carefully.
criteria.C5: Your report uses clear headings and IEEE-style references, but it lacks an abstract, figures or tables, and contains several typos and language errors. Add the abstract, use visual elements to support your discussion, proofread carefully, and complete the incomplete references to reach a higher level.
